blocks.body:
**Executive dashboard · Page 2 of 3**  
[1. Marketplace Overview](page_1_marketplace_overview.html) · **2. Marketplace Efficiency** · [3. Growth Quality & Operating Priorities](page_3_operating_priorities.html)

## Regional diagnosis

The operating-priority proxy identifies **23 taxi zones** with **2.99M completed trips**, or **19.5%** of May 2026 city volume. LaGuardia and JFK rank first and second by estimated excess Request-to-Pickup burden, together accounting for roughly **1.27M excess minutes** versus the city average.

The matrix is the regional equivalent of a map for this management view: demand is encoded by bubble size, growth on the horizontal axis, service pressure on the vertical axis, and the operating segment by color. “Supply-constrained priority” is a prioritization label based on observed completed trips and wait performance—not proof of an underlying supply shortage.

query.description: Compares pickup zones on completed-trip demand, request-to-pickup, growth, and excess request-to-pickup burden.

metric_definitions.estimated_excess_request_to_pickup_minut: Eligible completed trips multiplied by the positive zone wait gap versus the city average.
metric_definitions.supply_constrained_priority: Top-quartile completed-trip demand with average request-to-pickup above the city benchmark; an operating proxy, not causal proof.
metric_definitions.scatter_population: Five-borough taxi zones with at least 500 completed trips in each comparison month and a valid May 2026 wait metric.
